newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on frost talk, conditions.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on frost talk, conditions.

text.p: Forecasts for frost this week in the U.S. Midwest and concern USDA will reduce the condition ratings for the U.S. soybean crop boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"The frost talk and ideas for a poorer condition rating today, especially on beans brought beans and meal back," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Meteorologists early Monday said two cold weather systems were forecast for the U.S. Midwest this week with the first system expected to arrive late Monday.
Also, Friday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for below to much below normal tempeartures in the Midwest from September 26 through September 30.

Rosenthal Collins bought eight million bushels of November while Dean Witter Reynolds and Produce Grain each bought two million November, the traders said. Cargill Inc, Rand Financial and Lind Waldock each sold two million November, they said.
Soybeans closed 2-1/4 to 1/4 cents per bushel higher, with November up 3-1/2 at $7.98-3/4.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 37,000, down from 38,954 Friday.
In soybean options, Continental Grain bought 200 November $9.50 calls at 3/4 cent, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, down from 19,245 Friday.
